```{python}
import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# load data
data = pd.read_csv("data/college_football.csv")
```

```{python}
# plot of win pct vs recruiting rank
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(data["win_pct"], data["recruiting_rank"], c = data["year"], alpha = 0.65)
ax.set(xlabel="Win Percentage",
       ylabel="Recruiting Rank", title="Win-Percentage vs. Recruiting Rank")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# same plot but just picking 1 year
# create different data frames for each year
data2018 = data.loc[data["year"] == 2018].copy()
data2019 = data.loc[data["year"] == 2019].copy()
data2020 = data.loc[data["year"] == 2020].copy()
data2021 = data.loc[data["year"] == 2021].copy()
data2022 = data.loc[data["year"] == 2022].copy()
data2023 = data.loc[data["year"] == 2023].copy()
data2024 = data.loc[data["year"] == 2024].copy()

# actaully plot
# 2018
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(data2018["win_pct"], data2018["recruiting_rank"], alpha = 0.65)
ax.set(xlabel="Win Percentage",
       ylabel="Recruiting Rank", title="Teams in 2018")
plt.show()

# 2019
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(data2019["win_pct"], data2019["recruiting_rank"], alpha = 0.65)
ax.set(xlabel="Win Percentage",
       ylabel="Recruiting Rank", title="Teams in 2019")
plt.show()

# 2020
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(data2020["win_pct"], data2020["recruiting_rank"], alpha = 0.65)
ax.set(xlabel="Win Percentage",
       ylabel="Recruiting Rank", title="Teams in 2020")
plt.show()

# 2021
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(data2021["win_pct"], data2021["recruiting_rank"], alpha = 0.65)
ax.set(xlabel="Win Percentage",
       ylabel="Recruiting Rank", title="Teams in 2021")
plt.show()

# 2022
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(data2022["win_pct"], data2022["recruiting_rank"], alpha = 0.65)
ax.set(xlabel="Win Percentage",
       ylabel="Recruiting Rank", title="Teams in 2022")
plt.show()

# 2023
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(data2023["win_pct"], data2023["recruiting_rank"], alpha = 0.65)
ax.set(xlabel="Win Percentage",
       ylabel="Recruiting Rank", title="Teams in 2023")
plt.show()

# 2024
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(data2024["win_pct"], data2024["recruiting_rank"], alpha = 0.65)
ax.set(xlabel="Win Percentage",
       ylabel="Recruiting Rank", title="Teams in 2024")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# correlation between win percentage and recruiting rank
# in theory we should see a negative correlation (higher rank corresponds to lower number)

# overall
data["recruiting_rank"].corr(data["win_pct"])

## see if there is difference by year
# 2018
data2018["recruiting_rank"].corr(data2018["win_pct"])

# 2019
data2019["recruiting_rank"].corr(data2019["win_pct"])

# 2020
data2020["recruiting_rank"].corr(data2020["win_pct"])

# 2021
data2021["recruiting_rank"].corr(data2021["win_pct"])

# 2022
data2022["recruiting_rank"].corr(data2022["win_pct"])

# 2023
data2023["recruiting_rank"].corr(data2023["win_pct"])

# 2024
data2024["recruiting_rank"].corr(data2024["win_pct"])
```

```{python}
## look how it works within conferences
conf_corr = (
    data.groupby("conference")
    .apply(
        lambda g: g["win_pct"].corr(g["recruiting_rank"]),
        include_groups=False,
    )
    .reset_index(name="corr")
)

print(conf_corr)
```


```{python}
# how do the top 10 recruiting teams do in a given year?
top_10 = data[data["recruiting_rank"] <= 10]
print(top_10)

# see how many unique teams there are
top_10["team"].nunique()
# see how many unique conferences there are
top_10["conference"].nunique()

# how do the bottom 10 recruiting teams do in a given year?
bottom_10_by_year = (
    data.sort_values(["year", "recruiting_rank"])
    .groupby("year")
    .tail(10)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)

# check to make sure it grabbed 10 per year
print(bottom_10_by_year["year"].value_counts())

print(bottom_10_by_year.sort_values(
    ["win_pct", "year"], ascending = False))

```
